title: Documentation leaves the repository
what: Each file under docs/ is either removed, or its needed content moves where relay ships it (a command's --help, an error or refusal text, install.sh output, a plugin's skill or rule, the queue), or it stays with a stated reason. Readers of docs/ in code, hooks, skills and tests are changed to match.
why: Owner, 30 Oct: the vector is no documentation in the repository: what a person or an agent needs ships with relay itself (install.sh, `relay --help`, `relay setup --help`, error hints, plugin texts); "why" questions are answered by an agent reading the code and by the queue's recorded decisions; the handover's role goes to the queue or to local files. In line with the owner's manifesto of 29 Oct ("Никаких документаций, исключения - --help и подсказки в командах ... максимум ... краткий набор инструкций в README.md").
pass_cases: `ls docs` lists only files with a recorded reason to stay.
No hook, skill, test or program reads a removed file.
A fresh session can set up relay and answer "how does X work" from relay's own texts and code.

fact: Measured 30 Oct: `relay --help` prints 90 lines, a flat list of 35 command forms with their arguments (not one line per command); `relay <command> --help` prints that command's slice of the same hand-written text (queue 43 lines, check 23, setup 7, gate 7, bench 6, land 4), forms and flags on one line, no per-flag lines; 20 commands in bin/relay's dispatch table, `metrics` missing from help, and `relay metrics --help` prints the whole top-level help instead. README.md is 120 lines.

question: Where does the session state (today docs/handover.md, which relay setup writes into every project and relay doctor checks) live once docs/ leaves the repository?
options: a. keep it in the repository until the item that derives state from facts lands (recommended: measured, 20 of 28 recent owner decisions have no queue item to hold them)
b. a local file under $RELAY_HOME now, about 75 agent minutes (a guess); not in git, so not seen from other machines
c. no file; the queue alone, about 60 agent minutes (a guess); decisions about no item are lost at the next compaction

reading: a: the handover stays in the repository as it is for now.

fact: Front decision (owner can reverse; principle 9), from the reviewed design (rev 2, 30 Oct): docs leave file by file, the handover last. `relay --help` becomes one line per command (about 28 lines from 90; metrics shows; a test fails when a command takes more than one line); `relay <cmd> --help` and `relay help <cmd>` print the command's forms plus an optional long help kept in that command's own module, written only after the command leaves bin/relay (1,173 lines, over the 600 cap). docs/macos.md goes with speed-up-the-quick-gate; START_HERE.md removed; README cut to the install lines; plugins/relay/README.md (227 lines) moves into `relay gate --help` and kit.toml comments. Measured: Haiku answered design questions from the plugins at $0.027 in 29 turns. Estimate about 5 h of agent time (a guess).
